steps: Review the manufacturer's technical data sheet for switchgear SWG-01.
Visually inspect the physical nameplate on the main busbar section of the switchgear.
acceptance: The documented and physical busbar rating is 4000 A or greater.
reason: This test belongs to Level 1 as it involves verifying component specifications and physical nameplate data before installation and functional testing.

steps: Examine the factory test reports for UPS-02.
Verify the output capacity rating listed on the UPS module's identification plate.
acceptance: The rated output is confirmed to be at least 500 kW.
reason: Level 1 verification focus is on confirming that the individual equipment delivered matches the procurement and design specifications.

steps: Locate the manufacturer's nameplate on the GEN-01 alternator or enclosure.
Cross-reference the standby power rating with the approved submittal documentation.
acceptance: The nameplate confirms a standby rating of 1500 kW or greater.
reason: This test is categorized as Level 1 as it verifies the static capacity rating provided by the manufacturer.

steps: Retrieve the manufacturer data sheet for the generator to determine fuel consumption rate at 100% load.
Inspect the fuel storage tank nameplate or shop drawings to confirm total usable capacity.
Calculate total runtime by dividing usable capacity by the full-load consumption rate.
acceptance: The calculated runtime at full load must be at least 48 hours.
reason: This test belongs to Level 1 because it involves a review of design documentation and technical specifications to ensure capacity requirements are met.

steps: Inspect the physical nameplate of the ATS-01 unit installed on-site.
Cross-reference the nameplate data with the approved equipment submittals and electrical single-line diagrams.
acceptance: The ATS must have a continuous current rating of 2000 A or higher.
reason: This test is categorized as Level 1 because it confirms the static equipment ratings against the design requirements through document and visual verification.

steps: Perform a visual inspection of the circuit breaker BRK-05 faceplate to identify the trip unit or frame rating.
Verify that the installed rating matches the specification provided in the electrical schedule.
acceptance: The circuit breaker must be rated for exactly 630 A.
reason: This test belongs to Level 1 because it verifies that the specific component provided matches the design criteria through simple inspection and documentation review.

steps: Review the manufacturer's short-circuit test certification for BRK-05.
Submit the breaker to a third-party laboratory for high-current injection testing at 50 kA.
Inspect the breaker contacts and casing for structural integrity after the trip event.
acceptance: The breaker successfully interrupts a 50 kA fault current without sustaining external damage or failure.
reason: This test verifies the physical design rating of a standalone component at the equipment level prior to installation.

steps: Run CHL-01 in a controlled factory test environment at full load conditions.
Measure the chilled water flow rate and the temperature difference between the inlet and outlet.
Calculate the total cooling capacity in kW based on the measured thermal data.
acceptance: The calculated cooling capacity is at least 1200 kW.
reason: This test confirms that the specialized equipment meets its specific performance ratings at the manufacturer's facility.

steps: Operate the chiller at 100% cooling load for a minimum of 30 minutes.
Record the electrical power input (kW) using the power meter.
Calculate cooling output using the measured chilled water flow and temperature differential.
Divide the cooling output by the power input to determine the COP.
acceptance: The calculated Coefficient of Performance (COP) must be 5.5 or higher.
reason: This test verifies the actual operational efficiency of the equipment under load, which is characteristic of Level 4 functional performance testing.

steps: Locate the manufacturer's technical data sheet for PMP-01.
Identify the rated pump head value provided in the certified submittal.
Confirm the head rating matches or exceeds the required specification.
acceptance: The documented rated head must be 30 m or higher.
reason: Verification of equipment ratings through design documentation and manufacturer data occurs at Level 1.

steps: Examine the physical nameplate on cooling tower CT-01.
Cross-reference the nameplate data with the factory test report provided by the supplier.
Confirm that the heat rejection capacity is clearly stated.
acceptance: The nameplate or factory test report must show a heat rejection capacity of at least 1500 kW.
reason: This test validates the specified design capacity of the component at the procurement and factory documentation level.

steps: Obtain the technical specification sheet for CRAH-01 from the manufacturer.
Verify the rated total cooling capacity under design operating conditions.
acceptance: The documented cooling capacity of CRAH-01 is 100 kW or greater.
reason: Level 1 testing focuses on the verification of equipment specifications and factory-provided documentation before installation.

steps: Run the cooling plant at its maximum required facility load.
Manually shut down one operational chiller (CHL-01) to simulate a failure.
Monitor the remaining chillers to ensure they pick up the load without a loss in cooling capacity.
acceptance: The cooling plant maintains 100% of the required cooling load after the standby chiller takes over.
reason: Level 5 testing involves integrated system testing to verify that the redundant components function together as a system.

steps: Initiate a simulated utility power failure to trigger a transfer to generator power.
Start a stopwatch the moment the Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) completes the transfer to the generator.
Stop the timer when CHL-01 confirms compressor restart and begins active cooling.
acceptance: The time elapsed from power transfer to cooling resumption is 120 seconds or less.
reason: Level 5 testing validates the interoperability of the electrical and cooling systems during a site-wide power transition.

steps: Apply the full design heat load to the data center using load banks.
Induce a single point of failure in the cooling distribution path, such as closing a critical valve or tripping a pump breaker.
Observe if the system maintains the design load without any degradation in cooling performance.
acceptance: The cooling capacity remains at 100% of the design load despite the induced single failure.
reason: Level 5 is the appropriate stage for verifying Tier IV fault tolerance through comprehensive failure mode testing of the integrated environment.
